title: Exchange-Rate Pass-Through (ERPT) to Inflation Analysis for Colombia in Stata
goal: Study the exchange-rate pass-through (ERPT) relationship between the nominal exchange rate and inflation in Colombia, testing whether Claude can gather the required data, guide the full econometric analysis in Stata, and produce a reproducible Stata .do file, Excel workbook, and PowerPoint report end to end.
context: This project aims to test how powerful Claude can be when used as an AI assistant for an econometric analysis from start to finish. The main goal is to study the relationship between exchange-rate movements and inflation in Colombia while asking Claude to find and organize the required datasets from official sources, guide the analysis in Stata, explain the econometric decisions, and help reproduce the full model. The project will also test whether Claude can support the creation of reproducible outputs, including a Stata .do file, an Excel workbook, and a PowerPoint report, while keeping the analysis clear, consistent, and easy to reproduce.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes. While Claude successfully guided the entire step-by-step econometric workflow—providing exact Stata syntax, interpreting diagnostic tests, and structuring the final report—the data gathering could not be completed directly through Claude and required manual extraction from BanRep/DANE, and the generated Excel outputs had minor inaccuracies .

Step 1.step_action: Ask Claude to obtain and organize the monthly Colombian exchange-rate and CPI data required for the analysis, using Banco de la Republica and DANE as the primary data sources; identify official series, retrieve observations, verify monthly frequency, and format for Stata import.

nodes.label: Compose detailed role as Senior Macro-Econometrician and Stata expert and rules prompt for Claude
nodes.detail: The participant types a long instruction on the Claude desktop app home screen, telling Claude to act as a Senior Macro-Econometrician and Stata expert co-piloting an ERPT-to-inflation analysis for Colombia. She lists five ground rules (exact executable Stata syntax only, explain econometric logic accessibly, help select/verify clean variables, interpret diagnostics when pasted back, and help structure findings into Excel/PowerPoint) plus two extra rules: flag any uncertain data, and prioritize reproducible simplicity over unnecessary complexity.

nodes.label: Acknowledge role and ask grounding questions about model specification, frequency, and data-sourcing strategy
nodes.detail: Claude confirms it will act as the Stata co-pilot for the ERPT project, one step at a time, and before generating any code asks grounding questions about model specification (VAR vs. ARDL vs. single-equation), frequency, and data-sourcing strategy.

nodes.label: Request official monthly Colombian CPI/exchange-rate series identification
nodes.detail: Skips the uestion and tells Claude to begin Step 1 (data acquisition), asking it to identify the exact official series from Banco de la Republica/DANE for headline CPI/inflation and the nominal exchange rate (COP/USD TRM), plus any other recommended control variables, and to specify where it gathered the data from.

nodes.label: Perform live web search and produce a mixed-source recommended series table
nodes.detail: Claude states it will pull current official series identifiers, runs multiple web searches ('Searched the web - 2 notes'), and returns a 'Recommended Series (Official Sources)' table with 7 rows. Rows 1-5 are legitimate DANE/BanRep series (IPC base-2018, TRM), but rows 6-7 list a Brent crude oil ticker (DCOILBRENTEU) and US FRED series (CPIAUCSL, FEDFUNDS) as 'control' variables presented in the same official-looking table, even though Claude's own source column notes them as 'FRED (external, not BanRep/DANE)' -- a confident-looking but source-mixing/misleading presentation.

nodes.label: Reject Claude's sourced list and identify it as hallucinating, and upload own pre-prepared Excel dataset
nodes.detail: The participant reviews the recommended-series table on screen, scrolls through it, and pastes the manually-calculated inflation to Claude, and opens Windows File Explorer to her 'Ai_client > Project 2' folder and launches her own already-prepared Excel file containing Colombian IPC and TRM data from January 2003 onward, with pre-computed ln_IPC/ln_TRM log transforms and Inflation/Depreciation difference columns, and pastes/uploads this data to Claude in place of its web-sourced list.

nodes.label: Review and verify quality of the uploaded dataset, and ask clarifying questions
nodes.detail: Claude reviews the pasted data and flags several legitimate, non-alarming items, and asks clarifying questions about TRM frequency and

nodes.label: Read Claude's review, skip the question, report that Claude is hallucinating
nodes.detail: The participant opens the own already-prepared Excel file containing Colombian IPC and TRM data from January 2003 onward, reporting that Claude's flags on control variables are hallucinating

Step 2.step_name: Data Import, Time-Series Setup & Variable Construction
Step 2.step_action: Import the dataset into Stata, establish the monthly time-series structure, inspect for missing/inconsistent observations, and generate the inflation and exchange-rate depreciation variables required for the econometric analysis.

nodes.label: Manually import the excel dataset into Stata and run the data summarization code
Request exact Stata data-prep syntax
nodes.detail: The participant asks Claude for the exact executable Stata commands to clear memory, set up the environment, convert the date variable into a proper monthly Stata date format via tsset, and generate the key analytical variables (annualized monthly inflation, monthly exchange-rate depreciation, year-over-year log transforms), explicitly instructing Claude not to go beyond this step.

nodes.label: Write structured .do file for import, tsset, and variable generation
nodes.detail: Claude first checks whether a file was actually uploaded, then writes a .do file importing data/colombia_erpt_raw.xlsx, renaming variables to a lowercase convention (date_raw, ipc, trm) while preserving originals, converting date to mdate = mofd(date_d), running a duplicates/gap check, and declaring tsset mdate, monthly.

nodes.label: Read the code, paste and run rename and tsset commands in Stata and report the error message
nodes.detail: The participant pastes the rename and tsset codes into a new do file and runs the code in Stata; tsreport command meets an error, and pastes the error messageback to Claude

nodes.label: Confirm clean panel and correct tsreport command as an optional check
nodes.detail: Claude confirms the tsset result is good news for a clean panel and correct the code for tsreport and state it is an additional belt-and-suspenders gap check, noting it is a user-written command requiring ssc install if not already present.

nodes.label: Try the corrected code, get an error, and ask whether skipping is fine
nodes.detail: Running tsreport fails because it is not a Stata built-in, and the participant's ssc install tsreport attempt fails with a network/proxy error ('proxy host not found'), the same issue seen in session 1. She asks Claude, 'is it ok just to skip that?'

nodes.label: Confirm it is fine to skip tsreport and provide a manual gap-check fallback
nodes.detail: Claude confirms skipping is fine since tsset already confirmed no gaps, and offers a manual gap_check using only built-in Stata commands (gen gap_check = mdate - mdate[_n-1]) as a no-installation-needed alternative.

nodes.label: Paste and run variable-generation code from b2 and paste back the stata log
nodes.detail: The participant runs the diagnostic/log-level regeneration code and then a combined summarize across all eight series, pasting the describe output back to Claude showing 276 observations with plausible ranges (e.g., ipc mean 89.18, trm mean 2823.35).

nodes.label: Verifying the generated variables output is ok
Paste and run data description/summarization code from b2 and paste back the stata log
Interpret describe/summarize output and confirm readiness for regression
nodes.detail: Claude interprets the diagnostic and summarize output, confirming the panel is intact with 276 observations, properly time-indexed, and ready for the baseline regression, after which the participant says 'Moving to the 3rd step.'

nodes.label: Briefly read claude's interpretation and confirm the step is complete

Step 3.step_action: Estimate a baseline OLS regression to evaluate the relationship between exchange-rate depreciation and inflation in Colombia, focusing on sign, magnitude, significance, and explanatory power of the exchange-rate coefficient.

nodes.label: Ask for baseline static OLS specification
nodes.detail: The participant tells Claude the data is fully prepped and asks it to recommend a baseline static OLS specification modeling CPI inflation as a function of nominal exchange-rate depreciation and to provide the exact regress syntax.

nodes.label: Explain baseline specification and provide the regression syntax
nodes.detail: Claude begins explaining the standard static contemporaneous specification from the ERPT literature, starting to drift into additional commentary/context before giving just the command.

nodes.label: Read the syntax, instruct Claude to just run the OLS and not to skip any step
Provide the regress command only
nodes.detail: Claude responds 'Understood' and provides just the baseline OLS step -- regress inflation_mom depreciation_mom -- with no extra commentary beyond what's needed to run it.

nodes.label: Paste the baseline OLS regression syntax into Stata do fileand, run it, and paste output back to Claude
nodes.detail: The participant runs regress inflation_mom depreciation_mom in Stata (visible switching via the window-switcher among Claude, Stata/IC 15.1, the Do-file Editor, and Zoom windows) and pastes the output back to Claude: coefficient -0.0061552, Std. Err. 0.0073086, t=-0.84, p=0.400, R-squared=0.0026.

nodes.label: Interpret null/insignificant contemporaneous result as expected in ERPT literature
nodes.detail: Claude interprets the result as statistically insignificant and near zero (coefficient -0.0062, p=0.400, R2=0.26%), explaining this is a common, expected finding in the ERPT literature since pass-through is rarely contemporaneous (menu costs, waiting to see if depreciation is persistent), framing the null result as motivation to move to a dynamic/distributed-lag specification next, then stops as instructed to await the next step.

nodes.label: Read claude's interpretation and confirm the step is complete

Step 4.step_action: Conduct post-estimation diagnostic tests on the baseline OLS model to assess heteroskedasticity or serial correlation, using Claude to guide the appropriate Stata tests and interpret whether conventional OLS standard errors are reliable.

nodes.label: Ask for critical diagnostic tests needed and the syntax
nodes.detail: The participant asks Claude to identify the critical time-series diagnostic tests needed for this regression, naming stationarity/unit-root (dfuller), autocorrelation (estat dwatson / estat bgodfrey), and heteroskedasticity tests.

nodes.label: Provide dfuller, dwatson, bgodfrey and heteroskedasticity test syntax
nodes.detail: Claude provides a Stata block running dfuller on the differenced inflation_mom/depreciation_mom series, re-running the baseline regression to keep it in memory, then estat dwatson and estat bgodfrey with lags(1 2 3 4 6 12), and a heteroskedasticity test.

nodes.label: Run diagnostic tests in Stata and paste results
nodes.detail: The participant pastes the syntax for each test into Stata do file and runs the commands one by one, and pastes the results back.

nodes.label: Interpret diagnostics and produce verdict summary table
nodes.detail: Interprets the diagnostics, produces a verdict table (stationarity OK, autocorrelation severe, heteroskedasticity borderline), and recommends a distributed-lag or ECM spec next because ERPT is not contemporaneous.

nodes.label: Read claude's interpretation, judge that the autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity issues are acceptable.

Step 5.step_action: Extend the baseline model by incorporating lags of exchange-rate depreciation to examine delayed effects on inflation, then estimate the preferred specification using Newey-West standard errors and compare with the baseline OLS model.

nodes.label: Request dynamic distributed-lag model and Newey-West syntax
nodes.detail: The participant asks Claude to (1) evaluate whether the model has serial correlation, heteroskedasticity, or non-stationarity issues, (2) extend into a dynamic distributed-lag model adding lags 1-6 of exchange-rate depreciation, and (3) provide exact syntax to re-estimate using Newey-West standard errors (newey).

nodes.label: Write distributed-lag regression and Newey-West re-estimation code
nodes.detail: Claude writes a distributed-lag regression of inflation_mom on depreciation_mom and its lags 1 through 6, followed by a Newey-West re-estimation with lag(6) HAC correction, plus a joint significance test (test) and a cumulative-effect lincom summing the contemporaneous term and all six lag coefficients.

nodes.label: Run Newey-West distributed-lag model in Stata and paste results
nodes.detail: The participant pastes and runs the major part of the provided syntax in Stata and pastes the full output back to Claude.

nodes.label: Interpret distributed-lag results as mixed but informative delayed pass-through
nodes.detail: Claude interprets the individual lag coefficients: contemporaneous through L4 are insignificant, but L5 (0.0132, p=0.039) and L6 (0.0178, p=0.023) are significant at 5%, describing a delayed pass-through pattern. However the joint F-test across all lags is not significant, and the cumulative six-month effect is about 4.6%, only marginally significant (p=0.068). Claude frames the overall result as 'mixed but informative' -- strengthening the case for delayed rather than contemporaneous pass-through, but not yet strong enough for confident policy claims -- and suggests a longer lag window or cointegration/ECM approach as next steps, then stops as instructed.

nodes.label: Read claude's interpretation, add that more control variables are needed to improve, which Claude doesn't mention

Step 6.step_action: Consolidate the complete econometric analysis into a reproducible Stata .do file, create an Excel workbook with key data and regression results, and produce a PowerPoint presentation summarizing the research question, methodology, results, diagnostics, robust estimation, and economic conclusions.

nodes.label: Paste full working .do file and ask for a clean consolidated version
nodes.detail: The participant pastes her full working .do file back to Claude (shown as a 'PASTED' attachment) and asks it to help build a clean final version covering everything.

nodes.label: Assemble consolidated master .do file
nodes.detail: Claude assembles a single reproducible script ('ERPT_Colombia_Master.do') covering Steps 1 through 5 exactly as run, with no new analysis added, ending with the distributed-lag Newey-West model, its test and lincom commands, and a log close.

nodes.label: Request a plain copy-paste version of the .do file
nodes.detail: The participant tries to load the file in Claude but fails, so asks Claude to provide a plain-text version of the .do file to copy-paste.

nodes.label: Provide plain-text .do file
nodes.detail: Claude provides the full master .do file as a single plain code block, ready for direct copy-paste into Stata.

nodes.label: Read claude's response, confirm it doesn't add any new things, paste into Stata and save the do file
Request final Excel and PowerPoint deliverables
nodes.detail: The participant asks Claude to create two final deliverables: (1) a simple-format Excel file with all the important data and results, and (2) a PowerPoint explaining the whole process, whether/why the results are accurate, what should be done next, and some Colombian economic background.

nodes.label: Build Excel workbook and PowerPoint slide deck and flag data-completeness limitation honestly
nodes.detail: Claude begins building the Excel workbook via a Python/openpyxl script, but pauses mid-task to explicitly flag that it only has the first ~4 rows of her 276-row dataset as literally pasted text (the rest was only ever described via summary statistics and regression output), stating it does not want to fabricate 272 rows of fake data into the deliverable, and will instead build the workbook with real results plus a clearly-flagged sample/template for the raw-data sheet.

nodes.label: Download and review final deliverables
nodes.detail: The participant downloads both files, reviews the Excel Workbook andPowerPoint slide deck, comments that he will not trust the data and graphs but the structure and interpretation in the slides is good, and saves the files.
nodes.softwares: Claude desktop app, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft PowerPoint

Step 1.step_action: Ask Claude to obtain and organize the monthly Colombian exchange-rate and CPI data required for the analysis, using Banco de la Republica and DANE as the primary data sources; identify official series, retrieve observations, verify monthly frequency, and format for Stata import.
Step 1.input: A prompt to Claude specifying that the analysis concerns Colombia and requires monthly data for the COP/USD exchange rate from the Banco de la República and the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from DANE, together with the desired study period and the requirement to use the official sources rather than third-party databases.
Step 1.output: A single clean dataset containing the monthly date, Colombian exchange rate, and CPI observations, with the source and definition of each variable documented and the data formatted for direct use in Stata.
Step 1.tools: Claude, with access to the web and the official Banco de la República and DANE data sources.
rubrics: Both the exchange-rate and CPI series come directly from the specified official sources, with the exact source series and definitions clearly identified.
The dataset contains observations at a consistent monthly frequency over the complete selected study period, with dates correctly aligned between the two series.
The resulting dataset contains clearly labeled variables in appropriate units and is structured so that it can be imported directly into Stata.
Claude verifies the dataset for missing observations, duplicate months, inconsistent frequencies, and other obvious data-quality problems before presenting it as ready for analysis.
Claude documents the sources and data definitions sufficiently clearly that another researcher could reproduce the data-acquisition process.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The results were not as expected.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude was unable to gather the data independently, serving only to verify the dataset after it was manually retrieved and uploaded.

Step 2.step_name: Data Import, Time-Series Setup & Variable Construction
Step 2.step_action: Import the dataset into Stata, establish the monthly time-series structure, inspect for missing/inconsistent observations, and generate the inflation and exchange-rate depreciation variables required for the econometric analysis.
Step 2.input: The cleaned monthly dataset produced in Step 1 containing the date, exchange rate, and CPI series.
Step 2.output: A clean Stata dataset with a correctly defined monthly time-series structure and the derived inflation and exchange-rate depreciation variables, ready for the baseline econometric estimation.
rubrics: The monthly time-series structure is correctly declared in Stata, with dates properly ordered and no unexplained duplicate or missing periods.
Inflation and exchange-rate depreciation are correctly constructed from the CPI and exchange-rate series using economically appropriate transformations.
Summary statistics and basic time-series checks confirm that the resulting variables contain plausible values and are suitable for the subsequent econometric analysis.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The result was just as expected.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The Stata environment was set up seamlessly, correctly establishing the monthly time-series structure and generating accurate log-transformed variables for inflation and exchange-rate depreciation, with summary statistics confirming realistic values across all criteria

Step 3.step_action: Estimate a baseline OLS regression to evaluate the relationship between exchange-rate depreciation and inflation in Colombia, focusing on sign, magnitude, significance, and explanatory power of the exchange-rate coefficient.
Step 3.input: The cleaned and transformed Stata dataset from Step 2 containing inflation and exchange-rate depreciation.
Step 3.output: A baseline OLS regression result in Stata, together with an economic and statistical interpretation of the estimated relationship between exchange-rate depreciation and inflation.
rubrics: The regression correctly uses inflation as the dependent variable and exchange-rate depreciation as the main explanatory variable, with an economically appropriate baseline specification.
The coefficient's sign, magnitude, statistical significance, confidence interval, and model fit are correctly interpreted without making unsupported causal claims.

The results are clearly connected to the exchange-rate pass-through hypothesis, including an explicit assessment of whether the empirical evidence is consistent with a positive relationship between depreciation and inflation.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The baseline OLS model was correctly specified using monthly inflation as the dependent variable and exchange-rate depreciation as the main explanatory variable, with Stata output accurately interpreted across statistical significance, magnitude, and model fit while clearly validating the exchange-rate pass-through hypothesis

Step 4.step_action: Conduct post-estimation diagnostic tests on the baseline OLS model to assess heteroskedasticity or serial correlation, using Claude to guide the appropriate Stata tests and interpret whether conventional OLS standard errors are reliable.
Step 4.input: The baseline OLS regression and its residuals from Step 3.
Step 4.output: A set of Stata diagnostic test results and a concise assessment of whether heteroskedasticity and/or autocorrelation are present and whether a robust inference procedure is warranted.
rubrics: Appropriate tests for heteroskedasticity and serial correlation are correctly conducted on the baseline model.
Test statistics and p-values are correctly interpreted using appropriate null hypotheses and significance levels.
The findings are clearly translated into an econometric decision about whether conventional OLS standard errors are adequate or a robust/HAC inference method should be considered.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The AI helped me by doing the syntax for all of the tests asked.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The diagnostic phase was executed flawlessly, with Stata tests for heteroskedasticity and serial correlation properly implemented, null hypotheses and p-values accurately interpreted, and test results clearly translated into the necessary decision to adopt HAC standard errors for robust inference.

Step 5.step_action: Extend the baseline model by incorporating lags of exchange-rate depreciation to examine delayed effects on inflation, then estimate the preferred specification using Newey-West standard errors and compare with the baseline OLS model.
Step 5.input: The transformed Stata dataset, baseline OLS results, and diagnostic findings from Steps 3 and 4.
Step 5.output: A dynamic regression with the selected exchange-rate depreciation lags and Newey-West standard errors, accompanied by a comparison with the baseline OLS results and an assessment of whether the evidence for exchange-rate pass-through changes after accounting for time-series error characteristics.
rubrics: The selected lag structure is appropriately justified based on the economic mechanism and/or the diagnostic evidence rather than chosen arbitrarily.
Newey-West standard errors are correctly applied, and changes in coefficients, standard errors, statistical significance, and inference are accurately interpreted.
The final specification provides a clear assessment of whether exchange-rate depreciation has an immediate and/or delayed relationship with Colombian inflation.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The dynamic model was properly justified and Newey-West standard errors were accurately estimated, but the detailed assessment of immediate versus delayed pass-through impact (Rubric 3) was deferred to the final PowerPoint rather than fully addressed within this step.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude effectively guided the model extension, lag justification, and HAC error adjustments, successfully transitioning the analysis to its final presentation phase.

Step 6.step_action: Consolidate the complete econometric analysis into a reproducible Stata .do file, create an Excel workbook with key data and regression results, and produce a PowerPoint presentation summarizing the research question, methodology, results, diagnostics, robust estimation, and economic conclusions.
Step 6.input: The Stata dataset, regression outputs, diagnostic results, Newey-West estimates, and interpretations generated throughout Steps 1–5.
Step 6.output: A complete Stata .do file documenting the analysis from data preparation through final estimation, an Excel workbook organizing the relevant data and empirical results, and a PowerPoint report presenting the methodology, findings, interpretation, and limitations of the exchange-rate pass-through analysis.
Step 6.tools: Stata, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft PowerPoint, Claude.
rubrics: The Stata .do file contains the complete analytical workflow and can reproduce the main results from data preparation through the final econometric specification.
The Excel workbook accurately organizes the relevant data and key empirical results, with numerical values consistent with the Stata output.

The PowerPoint clearly presents the research question, methodology, main findings, diagnostic results, robust estimation, economic interpretation, and key limitations without making unsupported causal claims.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The Stata .do file and PowerPoint deck were fully accurate and comprehensive, but the Excel workbook contained minor numerical and structural inaccuracies that required manual corrections.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude successfully delivered a fully reproducible Stata script and a complete, well-structured presentation of the econometric analysis, though the Excel summary tables needed minor manual adjustments for complete accuracy.
